# Dual-Axis Ultra-Review — Consolidated Lead Report
**Repo:** f:/Dev/GH/cesium-webgpu · **HEAD:** f6fd367827 (Batch 220) · **Date:** 2026-06-11
**Axis A:** WebGPU-renderer vs our-WebGL (parity / decisions / backport / architecture / performance)
**Axis B:** our-WebGL vs upstream CesiumGS/cesium (fork drift)
**Merge-base:** 0becdbfc17 · **upstream/main:** 467919ca90 (284 ahead / 435 of ours)

---

## 1. Executive Summary

**Port health (Axis A): functional but with a cluster of latent CRITICAL/HIGH correctness gaps concentrated in picking, post-process, and the model PBR path.** The WebGPU renderer is broad and architecturally sound (clean GraphicsContext abstraction, device-loss recovery, a faithful command-variant dispatcher), but four classes of defect recur:

1. **Feature-detection by `defined()` instead of capability** — `PickDepth.update` branches on `defined(context.readPixels)`, which is *true* on WebGPU (the method exists and returns null), so the entire async depth-readback path is never reached and **`pickPosition` returns undefined on WebGPU** (CRITICAL). This poisons ray-pick, sampleHeight, clampToHeight, and the pickPosition cache.
2. **Hardcoded/placeholder values that were "to be overridden" and never were** — OIT composite pipeline pinned to `rgba8unorm` (fails validation against the bgra8/rgba16f scene color, CRITICAL); tonemapper reads a non-existent `_tonemapping.type` and always falls back to PBR_Neutral (HIGH); built-in bloom/AO/DoF/godray allocate 8-bit intermediates in HDR mode, clamping highlights before tonemap (HIGH).
3. **Parity drift in shading math not forced by the backend** — specular IBL uses analytic Fresnel instead of the generated-but-unconsumed BRDF LUT split-sum (HIGH); IBL cubemaps sampled in raw eye space (reflections swim, MEDIUM); CSM drops the soft-shadow PCF kernel the single-map path keeps (HIGH); Gaussian-splat back-to-front sort silently dropped (HIGH).
4. **Per-frame allocation hot paths** — globe surface renderer builds 3-4 bind groups *per tile per pass per frame* with no cache (HIGH); billboard/label rebuild and re-upload the entire instance buffer every frame while the Point renderer already has the dirty-gate fix (HIGH).

**Fork drift posture (Axis B): trending merge-hostile, driven almost entirely by a single 657-file ES6-modernization mega-commit, not by WebGPU integration.** The genuine WebGPU value across the most-churned Scene/Renderer/Widgets files is a handful of FeatureRenderer hook-lines; it rides on top of ~30,000+ lines of whole-file `function→class` + `defineProperties→get/set` rewrites and decompositions of files upstream still actively maintains. Today the conflict surface is *latent* (upstream touched almost none of these files since merge-base), so syncs are clean by luck — but the next upstream patch to Scene.js, Model.js, Globe.js, Cesium3DTileset.js, or any collection file will not 3-way-merge and must be hand-reapplied into the class form. **The drift is reducible:** a large fraction (I3SNode, VoxelEllipsoidShape, Cesium3DTileStyle, the animation widgets, the inspector ViewModels, MetadataClassProperty, SampledProperty, TerrainEncoding, Texture, TextureAtlas) is *pure cosmetic conversion of files with no WebGPU hook*, directly violating the project's own "NEVER modernize a file you're not otherwise touching" rule. The mega-commit also shipped real regressions (`Resource.contains`, `TimeIntervalCollection.contains`, the Animation.js childNodes text-node bug) — predictable fallout of an unreviewable codemod-scale commit — and dropped ~80% of public-API JSDoc/@example blocks on Camera/SSCC.

**Biggest themes:** (a) *capability-vs-existence* feature detection is the single highest-leverage correctness root-cause; (b) *generated-but-unconsumed* resources (BRDF LUT, ID target, derived-command flags, ground-atmosphere buffer) form a pattern of misleading scaffolding whose docstrings overstate wiring; (c) *uncached per-frame bind-group/buffer churn* is the dominant perf regression vs WebGL's in-place state model; (d) *blanket modernization* is the dominant — and largely avoidable — driver of merge cost.

**Is drift sustainable?** Not on the current trajectory. It is recoverable cheaply: revert the ~15 pure-cosmetic conversions (≈ tens of thousands of conflict-lines for zero functional loss), document a Scene→companion-file MOVE-MAP in the sync runbook, and gate future modernization behind an actual hook. With those, future syncs return to mostly fast-forward.

## 2. CRITICAL & HIGH Findings (Axis A), grouped by theme

### Theme 1 — Picking is broken on WebGPU (capability-vs-existence)

**A6.1 · PickDepth feature-detection picks the WebGL branch on WebGPU → pickPosition returns undefined · CRITICAL · port-regression**
Files: `PickDepth.js:103,125`, `WebGPUContext.ts:2533`, `WebGPUSceneRendererFrustumLoop.ts:643`
Issue: `update()` branches on `if (defined(context.readPixels))`; WebGPUContext.readPixels is a real method returning null, so the WebGL framebuffer path runs, `_asyncDepthTexture` is never set, and `getDepth()` returns undefined. `pickPositionWorldCoordinates()` always returns undefined on WebGPU (verified: both branch sites at :103/:125 gate on `defined(context.readPixels)`).
Fix: Add a `context.supportsSyncReadback` capability getter (true on WebGL, false on WebGPU) OR leave `readPixels` inherited-undefined on WebGPUContext so existing `defined()` checks resolve as the async authors intended. Then verify via a Playwright depth-pick probe.

**A6.2 · readCenterPixel returns stale prior-frame pixels → pickMetadata/pickVoxelCoordinate broken · HIGH · port-regression**
Files: `WebGPUPickFramebuffer.ts:413-423`, `Picking.js:343-471`
Issue: `readCenterPixel()` reads only `_lastReadPixels` from a prior fire-and-forget readback; the synchronous metadata/voxel pick paths call it *before* `endFrame()` submits the current pick render.
Fix: Add a synchronous-after-submit center-pixel readback OR async `pickMetadataAsync`/`pickVoxelCoordinateAsync` mirroring `endAsync`. Add a one-time warning + DEFERRED_WORK entry.

**A6.3 · Ray picks (pickFromRay/sampleHeight/clampToHeight) call end() synchronously → stale results · HIGH · port-regression**
Files: `PickingRayHelpers.js:220,226-227`, `Picking.js`
Issue: `getRayIntersection` uses sync `pickFramebuffer.end()` (returns previous frame's pixels by design) and expects `getDepth()` to return a number (it returns undefined per A6.1). No async ray-pick path exists.
Fix: Add an async ray-pick path (offscreen render + `endAsync` + awaited getDepth) analogous to `drillPickAsync`; route sampleHeight/clampToHeight through it; add the same oneTimeWarning drillPick has.

**A6.4 · endAsync shares `_stagingBuffer` with `_startReadback` but ignores `_readbackInFlight` · MEDIUM**
Files: `WebGPUPickFramebuffer.ts:336-407,429-504`
Issue: `endAsync` encodes into the same buffer and maps it without the in-flight guard; a sync pick (hover) followed by an async pick (click) can hit "buffer used in submit while mapped".
Fix: Make `endAsync` respect/set `_readbackInFlight`, or allocate a per-call staging buffer like WebGL's PBO path.

> Note: A6 picking findings are interlocking — fix A6.1 first; A6.5 (`_pickPositionCache` caching undefined-in-flight) and several stale DEFERRED_WORK entries (DP-H45, DP-H46) are largely subsumed by it.

### Theme 2 — Post-process: hardcoded formats and broken user-facing controls

**A8.1 · OIT MRT composite pipeline hardcoded to `rgba8unorm` — pipeline validation fails on every MRT-OIT frame · CRITICAL · port-regression**
Files: `WebGPUOIT.ts:295,222`, `WebGPUSceneRendererTranslucentPass.ts`, `WebGPUContext.ts:389`
Issue: `_createCompositePipeline` builds with `format: "rgba8unorm"` ("Will be overridden at draw time" — verified at :295, never is); `executeComposite` ignores its `targetFormat` param. Scene color is bgra8unorm (SDR) / rgba16float (HDR), so the composite pass fails WebGPU's format-match rule whenever a command populates `_oitPipeline` (Gaussian splats + explicit opt-ins).
Fix: Cache the composite pipeline per target format keyed on `_sceneColorFormat`; thread `targetFormat` into pipeline creation; rebuild on HDR toggle.

**A8.2 · Tonemapper reads non-existent property — user's `scene.postProcessStages.tonemapper` always ignored · HIGH · port-regression**
Files: `WebGPUPostProcessStageCollection.ts:174-190`, `Tonemapper.js`
Issue: `mapTonemapType` reads `collection._tonemapping?.type ?? collection._tonemappingType` (verified at :175); neither exists. The real selector is the string `_tonemapper`. `type` is always undefined → always `default → PBR_NEUTRAL`. Setting `Tonemapper.ACES` is a silent no-op.
Fix: Read the `collection.tonemapper` string and map REINHARD/MODIFIED_REINHARD/FILMIC/ACES/PBR_NEUTRAL → TonemapMode. Add a unit test. (The numeric-case mapping is actually internally correct — the *only* bug is the always-undefined read.)

**A8.3 · Built-in Bloom/AO/DoF/GodRay allocate 8-bit intermediates in HDR mode · HIGH · port-regression**
Files: `WebGPUPostProcessPipeline.ts:703-836`, `WebGPUBloomEffect.ts`, `WebGPUAmbientOcclusionEffect.ts`
Issue: `addBloom/addAmbientOcclusion/addDepthOfField/addGodRay` pass `canvasFormat` (SDR) instead of `_intermediateFormat` (rgba16float in HDR); each effect builds its textures in that format, clamping HDR >1.0 highlights before tonemap — defeating bloom's purpose. The user-stage path was fixed for this (Batch 199 B198-D1) but built-ins were left behind.
Fix: Pass `this._intermediateFormat` to all four; add an HDR bloom probe to visual-regression.

**A8.4 · Bloom mis-maps WebGL brightness/contrast onto a luminance threshold (and inverts the default) · HIGH · port-regression**
Files: `WebGPUPostProcessStageCollection.ts:223,313`, `WebGPUBloomEffect.ts`, `BrightPass.wgsl`
Issue: Maps `bloomThreshold = bloom.uniforms.brightness` and feeds it as a BrightPass luminance threshold. WebGL `brightness` defaults to **-0.3** as an HSB add in a contrast-bias pre-stage — so the default makes threshold negative → everything passes; `contrast` (128) is dropped (WGSL hardcodes 1.0). Two different algorithms.
Fix: Port the WebGL contrast/brightness/HSB bright-pass semantics and map all six uniforms, or document the algorithm swap and at minimum stop feeding `brightness` as `threshold`.

**A8.5 · User GLSL post-process stages silently dropped in production (warning is pragma-stripped) · HIGH · port-regression**
Files: `WebGPUPostProcessStageCollection.ts:465-477`, `WebGPUUserPostProcessStage.ts`
Issue: Any stage without a `wgslFragmentShader` uniform (the entire PostProcessStageLibrary: BlackAndWhite, Brightness, NightVision, LensFlare, Silhouette) is counted glslOnly and dropped. The only signal is a `oneTimeWarning` wrapped in `//>>includeStart('debug')` — stripped from production. (The GLSL-drop is tracked as NEW-POSTPROCESS-USER-WGSL; the production-silence and library breadth are NOT.)
Fix: Move the warning out of the debug pragma (it's a real functionality loss, not a per-frame diagnostic).

### Theme 3 — Model PBR / IBL parity drift (not forced by WebGPU)

**A3.1 · Specular IBL uses analytic Fresnel instead of split-sum BRDF-LUT; the LUT is generated every device-init but never consumed by the model path · HIGH · port-regression**
Files: `ModelPBRComplete.wgsl:2640,2698-2702,2652`, `WebGPUBrdfLutGenerator.ts`, `WebGPUImageBasedLighting.ts:15-16`
Issue: FS computes `kS_ibl = fresnelSchlickRoughness(...)`, no BRDF-LUT term, no FmsEms multi-scatter. `buildModelIBLEntries` binds 4 entries with no LUT slot; `brdfLut` is referenced only in DeferredLighting.wgsl. The IBL docstring falsely claims model split-sum uses the LUT. Metals/rough dielectrics read brighter/dimmer and lose energy conservation.
Fix: Bind the LUT into the model material bind group (free group-1 slot) and replace the analytic term with `radiance * (F * brdfLut.x + brdfLut.y)` + FmsEms/dielectricScattering — wiring, not new infra. (DEFERRED_WORK:669-680's "split-sum shipped Batch 130" claim covers only the SH/cubemap diffuse path and is overstated.)

**A3.2 · IBL cubemaps sampled in raw eye space — reflections rotate with the camera · MEDIUM · port-regression**
Files: `ModelPBRComplete.wgsl:2650,2659,2699`, `ImageBasedLightingStageFS.glsl:66,92`
Issue: Diffuse N and specular R sampled in eye space; WebGL applies `model_iblReferenceFrameMatrix`. Cubemaps are world-aligned (sourced from specularEnvironmentMaps / procedural sky), so the escape-hatch "moot if baked in eye space" does NOT apply — reflections swim as the camera orbits.
Fix: Pass the IBL reference-frame matrix into the camera/material UBO and apply to N and R before sampling.

**A3.3 · Direct-light geometry term diverges (Schlick-GGX k=(r+1)²/8 vs height-correlated Smith-joint; f90=1.0 vs clamp(reflectance·25)) · MEDIUM · port-regression**
Files: `ModelPBRComplete.wgsl:852-866,2241`, `pbrLighting.glsl:56-69,134`
Fix: Port `smithVisibilityGGX` and `f90 = clamp(czm_maximumComponent(F0)*25, 0, 1)` into the WGSL.

**A3.4 · VS runs full prev-frame morph+skin+instance deformation unconditionally even when TAA off · MEDIUM · port-regression**
Files: `ModelPBRComplete.wgsl:772-814`
Issue: `prevPositionMC` recompute (~doubles per-vertex deformation on skinned/morphed rigs) has no motion-flag guard though the FS gates motion *output* on `material.motionFlags.x`.
Fix: Gate the prev-pose block on `material.motionFlags.x > 0.5` (uniform branch, cheap).

**A3.5 · Merged material/instance/IBL bind groups rebuilt via createBindGroup every frame per primitive · MEDIUM (was HIGH) · port-regression**
Files: `WebGPUModelRenderer.js:2855-2866,3318`
Issue: Real per-frame allocation, but texture entries are already memoized on primCache and the rebuild over pre-built entry arrays is cheaper than implied; the anti-pattern is acknowledged in-comment.
Fix: Memoize merged BGs on primCache/nodeCache with a dirty flag (material buffer identity, texture refresh, IBL views, materialDefines).

### Theme 4 — Tiles / point-cloud / splat correctness

**A2.1 · Gaussian splats render in buffer order — CPU back-to-front sort silently dropped · HIGH · port-regression**
Files: `WebGPUGaussianSplatRenderer.ts:1037-1057,281-291`, `GaussianSplatPrimitive.js:1183-1192,2071-2102`
Issue: WebGPU draws `instanceCount: cache.splatCount` in storage order, never reading `primitive._indexes`; the JS `update()` early-returns before the sort state machine. Premultiplied over-blend is order-dependent → wrong tinting/haloing that changes with camera angle. (OIT variant mitigates *if* used, but the default color pipeline is order-dependent.)
Fix: Consume `_indexes` as a per-instance attribute/storage buffer (mirror WebGL), or implement the earmarked GPU radix sort feeding drawIndirect. At minimum let the CPU sort run. Fix DEFERRED_WORK:637 which misstates a sort exists.

**A2.2 · PointCloudLOD.wgsl slot-255 offset broadcast clobbers a compacted index when a workgroup is fully visible · HIGH**
Files: `PointCloudLOD.wgsl:150-156,257-271`
Issue: `sharedVisible[255u] = globalOffset` with comment "safe because localCount < 256", but at LOD-0 all 256 threads can be visible → the real index at slot 255 is overwritten; the writeback emits the offset as a point index. One wrong/duplicate point + one dropped per fully-visible LOD-0 workgroup; subgroup variant identical.
Fix: Use a dedicated `var<workgroup> wgOffset: u32` (or size sharedVisible to 257).

### Theme 5 — Globe surface & primitives

**A1.1 / A14.1 · Globe surface renderer allocates 3-4 GPUBindGroups per tile per pass per frame (no cache) · HIGH · port-regression**
Files: `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts:877-905,1302-1369`
Issue: bindGroup0 (camera+tile UB), bindGroup1 (`_createTextureBindGroup`, 17 entries + scratch array), bindGroup2 (water/ocean) all freshly allocated per visible tile per pass. ~600-800 GPUBindGroup objects/sec at 200 tiles. Texture *views* are cached; the bind groups are not. The Batch-55 effects-BG cache covers group3 only — groups 0/1/2 are uncovered and undocumented.
Fix: Cache group1/group2 per (tile id, imagery-set revision) / (waterMask id); for group0, switch to a `hasDynamicOffset:true` BGL so one cached BG is reused with the ring-allocator offset (see A14.7). Add getStats().

**A4.1 · WebGPUGroundAtmosphereRenderer produces an unbound buffer every frame — dead path · HIGH (functionality-gap)**
Files: `WebGPUGroundAtmosphereRenderer.ts:97-153`, `GroundAtmosphere.wgsl`, `Globe.js:1177-1178`, `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceCameraUB.ts`
Issue: `_webgpuAtmosphereBuffer` is only written and cleared — no pipeline binds it; `computeGroundAtmosphere()` is never imported by GlobeTerrain.wgsl. The live ground-atmosphere shading runs from camera-UB fields (GlobeTerrain.wgsl:3482-3500). The renderer's docstring falsely claims GlobeTerrain reads its buffer (superseded Session 65). FEATURE_INVENTORY:500 and MIGRATION_STATUS:2158 still mark it SHIPPED/Wired.
Fix: Delete the renderer + WGSL + Globe.js call + registration (real path already covers it), OR wire `_webgpuAtmosphereBuffer` into a real bind group. Update FEATURE_INVENTORY:500.

**A14.2 · Billboard + Label rebuild and re-upload the entire instance buffer every frame · HIGH · port-regression**
Files: `WebGPUBillboardRenderer.js:1251,156,1327`, `WebGPULabelRenderer.js:1012`, `WebGPUPointPrimitiveRenderer.js:959-965`
Issue: `buildInstanceData` allocates `Float32Array(length*44)` and full-uploads unconditionally — no dirty gate. WebGL writes only `_billboardsToUpdate` sub-ranges. The Point renderer already has the `needsRebuild` gate; Billboard/Label do not. Biggest collections regression for large static datasets.
Fix: Port the Point `needsRebuild` gate; keep `cache.instanceData`/`lastLength`; writeBuffer only dirty sub-ranges. (A14.9 is the dirty-region upload facet of the same fix.)

### Theme 6 — Shadows / clustered lighting

**A7.1 · CSM receive drops soft-shadow PCF + normal-shading that WebGL and the WebGPU single-map path both have · HIGH · port-regression**
Files: `ShadowReceiveCSM.wgsl:107`, `PrimitivePhongTexturedColor.wgsl` (sampleOneCascade:253-270, computeShadowFactor:342-343)
Issue: CSM uses a single `textureSampleCompareLevel` tap and ignores `effects.shadowSoftShadows` — but the single-map path in the *same file* branches on it to call a 3×3 PCF kernel. Enabling soft shadows softens single-map shadows but is a silent no-op for cascades.
Fix: Add a PCF branch to `sampleOneCascade` gated on `shadowSoftShadows` (comparison sampler is already PCF-ready); fold the normal-shading clamp into `computeShadowFactorCSM`.

### Theme 7 — Compute / perf infra & build

**A10.1 / A12.1 · Globe pass builds and discards a render bundle every frame instead of caching · HIGH (A10) / MEDIUM (A12, output-correct) · port-regression**
Files: `WebGPUSceneRendererGlobePass.ts:108-138`, `WebGPURenderBundleManager.ts`
Issue: Creates a fresh `GPURenderBundleEncoder`, replays every globe command, finishes, executes once, drops the bundle — re-encoded every frame above the count≥8 threshold. The `getOrCreate()` cache exists and is used correctly elsewhere (`WebGPUEnvironmentRenderer.js:1022`). Pays encode + bundle-build cost with zero replay amortization — plausibly net-negative vs plain executeBatch. FEATURE_INVENTORY:660 and FUTURE_RESEARCH assume amortization the code never achieves.
Fix: Route through `renderBundleManager.getOrCreate()` keyed on tile-set version + pass + format with invalidation on tile add/remove, OR drop the inline bundle path until a real caching strategy lands.

**A16.1 · Unconditional WebGPU cluster re-exports in engine index.js break the webgl-only variant build · HIGH (build-graph)**
Files: `scripts/build.js:496,502,1514,1520`, `scripts/bundleVariantPlugin.js`, `scripts/stubs/emptyModule.js`
Issue: `createIndexJs`/`createCesiumJs` emit 4 cluster re-exports + LightTypes constants unconditionally (verified at :496/:502/:1514/:1520); these files are NOT in `WEBGPU_COMPAT_EXEMPTIONS` (verified — only WebGLCompatibilityStub/WebGPUShaderTranslator/WebGLStubPipelineExtractor/WebGPUNagaTranspiler are). In webgl-only the alias plugin redirects them to `emptyModule.js` (default-only export), and ESM static named-export linking errors: "No matching export … for WebGPUClusterBoundsRenderer" (empirically reproduced in adjudication). The WGSL-preprocessor exports already engineer around this via `index-wgsl.js`; the cluster exports were added (Batch 147+) without that gating. The committed `CesiumWebGLOnly.js` is stale, so the break hasn't triggered yet — but a fresh `gulp buildCesiumWebGLOnly` regenerates the breaking barrel.
Fix: Move the 4 cluster re-exports + constants into `index-wgsl.js` (mirroring the preprocessor split). Add `gulp buildCesiumWebGLOnly` + `node Tools/variant-smoke-test.mjs` to CI (see A16.6).

**A11.1 · WebGPUDerivedCommand is orphaned scaffolding — flags never read, caches never populated, dispatcher has zero callers · HIGH (architecture)**
Files: `WebGPUDerivedCommand.ts`, `WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:3129`
Issue: `create*DerivedCommand` set `_logDepth/_pickMode/_hdrMode/_shadowMode/_depthOnly/_colorWriteMask/_cullMode/_depthBias` that no pipeline-build path reads; static caches written only by clearCache/getCacheStats; `createDerivedCommand` has zero callers; even `executeDepthOnlyBatch` is dead. Real derived-command realization is `selectCommandVariant` + LOG_DEPTH define + WebGPULogDepth.ts. FEATURE_INVENTORY:423 mislabels it `(SHIPPED)`, actively misleading readers.
Fix: Delete `WebGPUDerivedCommand.ts` + `createDerivedCommand` + spec (and the dead `clone()` in A11.2, and the no-op shadow-acne flags in A11.8), OR add an explicit "no-op pending" docstring + DEFERRED_WORK entry. Fix the FEATURE_INVENTORY tag.

## 3. Parity Drift — where WebGPU is NOT a faithful mirror of our WebGL (and shouldn't diverge)

These are algorithmic/behavioral divergences not forced by the backend — WebGPU should mirror WebGL:

| Drift | Severity | Anchor |
|---|---|---|
| Gaussian splats unsorted (premultiplied over-blend, order-dependent) | HIGH | A2.1 |
| Specular IBL analytic Fresnel vs split-sum BRDF-LUT | HIGH | A3.1 |
| CSM drops soft-shadow PCF + normal-shading the single-map path keeps | HIGH | A7.1 |
| IBL cubemaps sampled in eye space (no reference-frame matrix) | MEDIUM | A3.2 |
| Direct-light geometry term (Schlick-GGX vs Smith-joint; f90) | MEDIUM | A3.3 |
| OIT weight = McGuire Eq.9 + window-space z vs WebGL Eq.10 + view-space z; composite math + background-alpha rule differ | MEDIUM | A8.6 |
| Bloom algorithm + uniform mapping (HSB contrast/brightness vs luminance threshold) | HIGH | A8.4 |
| `useWebMercatorT` two-source-of-truth: tile-UB flag recomputed independently of the cache's `isMercator` return | MEDIUM | A1.4 |
| Clustered-light assign ignores cluster-bounds changes → stale bins on resize/FOV with no camera motion | MEDIUM | A7.2 |
| `applyPerEncoderState` skips `setStencilReference(0)` (latent; all live refs are 0xff) | LOW | A11.3 |
| Clearcoat Fresnel basis (VdotH vs NdotV) + direct-only dimming + missing coat IBL | LOW | A3.6 |
| disableDepthTestDistance forces clipPos.z=0 with no w≤0 guard | LOW | A5.7 |
| Depth-sample classifiers discard on exact `surfaceDepth == 0.0` + linear sampler on packed-RGBA depth | LOW | A4.6 |
| Grid/Checkerboard material thickness/AA uses viewport-ratio approximation, not fwidth() | LOW | A4.7 |
| `glCullFaceToGPU` maps FRONT_AND_BACK→'back' with no documented skip (unreachable in current scenes) | LOW | A11.5 |
| `webglToWebGPUBlendFactor` falls back to 'one' for CONSTANT_ALPHA (sibling converter handles it) | LOW | A11.6 |

Note: the per-model prev-frame clip in single-precision world space (A9.2) is a **recognized accepted approximation** (matches the Voxel TAA pattern in AUDIT_2026_05_02), downgraded to MEDIUM — the design doc names the RTE fix but error only shows as transient multi-pixel velocity noise during fast fly-to.

## 4. Questionable WebGPU Decisions to revisit for durability/correctness

- **A2.3 · DecoupledLookbackScan relies on inter-workgroup forward-progress + device-scope visibility WebGPU doesn't guarantee** (MEDIUM). `storageBarrier()` in a spin loop with no iteration cap → potential livelock when grid > occupancy. Opt-in (default off). Fix: gate behind a capability/occupancy check, or switch to a safe two-pass scan, **and** add an iteration-cap watchdog + console.error sentinel (currently missing, violating the infinite-loop-guard rule).
- **A10.2 · WebGPUBindGroupCache has no eviction despite docstring claiming "evicts the stale one lazily"** (MEDIUM). Only `invalidateAll()` removes entries; the only unbounded cache in a subsystem where pipeline/storage/resource pools are all LRU-bounded. Fix: add an insertion-order LRU (~256) like WebGPURenderPipelineCache, or correct the docstring contract.
- **A10.4 · Render-bundle eviction tick gated behind `perfManager._config.renderBundles`** (MEDIUM). Bundles are admitted independently of that flag (Environment renderer), so with the flag off `_currentFrame` never advances and `_evictStale` never fires — aging decoupled from use. Fix: drive `renderBundleManager.beginFrame()` from the unconditional per-frame boundary like `uniformAllocator.beginFrame()`.
- **A10.5 · WebGPUResourceManager sampler & BGL caches use `JSON.stringify` keys, never evict** (MEDIUM). Order-sensitive keys duplicate GPU objects; unbounded. Fix: deterministic field-ordered keys; soft cap on the BGL cache.
- **A11.4 · Pipeline cache key relies on caller-supplied `descriptor.name` to encode shader-variant identity** (LOW, downgraded). No shader-module/entryPoint in the key; correctness delegated to each caller's name string. Latent — harden with a WeakMap-id of vertex/fragment module + entryPoint.
- **A8.7 · OIT pipeline cache keyed on `shaderCode.length`** (LOW). Length+entry+label collision serves the wrong injected OIT module silently; label is often the owner class name (non-unique). Fix: FNV/DJB2 hash of the full source.
- **A8.8 · f16 tonemap error-scope is a no-op** (LOW). `pushErrorScope`/`popErrorScope` bracket no GPU work; the claimed f16→f32 next-frame fallback path does not exist (and FORK_FEATURE_INVENTORY:110 falsely claims it's verified). Fix: pick f32 source up front when device lacks shader-f16, remove the dead scope + misleading comment.
- **A11.7 · Shader-module cache key packs sourceId in 8 bits / defines in 24 with no overflow assert** (LOW). No bug today (sourceId≤33, defines≤bit15) but silent aliasing if the add-only registry crosses 256. Fix: debug-pragma overflow assert per the "permanent sentinels" rule.
- **A9.4 · TAA runs pre-tonemap on linear/HDR contradicting its own design doc** (MEDIUM). SDR-mode design says post-tonemap; code is pre-tonemap; HDR variance clamp un-retuned. Fix: decide deliberately and reconcile code ↔ TAA_DESIGN.md.
- **A5.6 · `updateWebGPUBillboards`/`updateWebGPUPolylines` declared `async` with no `await`** (LOW). Converts sync throws to unhandled rejections; falsely implies microtask deferral. Fix: drop `async` to match Point/Label.

## 5. Backport Opportunities (WebGPU-only → WebGL2), ranked

| Rank | Feature | WebGL2 mechanism | Value | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Precision-stable ray-sphere intersection** (1/radius-scaled) → `czm_raySphereIntersectionInterval.glsl` | Pure GLSL algebra, +1 divide/mul | Strict precision win for sky-atmosphere LUT, volumetric clouds, all ray-sphere consumers | **Very low** (~5 lines; existing atmosphere probes cover it) — A1.3 |
| 2 | **God rays / SSR / TAA** screen-space passes | Native fragment passes; `previousViewProjection` already in shared UniformState (A15.2) | High — closes the biggest post-process parity gap | Medium (TAA only needs jitter + GLSL reprojection FS since motion-vec infra is backend-neutral) |
| 3 | **Procedural volumetric clouds** | Pure fullscreen ray-march FS | High | Medium (100% backportable) |
| 4 | **Motion-vector / previousViewProjection infra** (de-risks TAA backport) | Already populated unconditionally on WebGL UniformState (verified getter at :423, update at :798) | Enabler | Trivial (verify, then add consuming stage) — A15.2 |
| 5 | **Forward+ clustered lighting** | Cluster-assign compute → WebGL2 fragment-pass rewrite | High | High (compute→fragment rewrite) |
| 6 | **IBL prefilter + atmosphere LUT** | Existing ComputeEngine fragment-to-texture path | Medium | Medium |
| 7 | **GPU within-tile point-cloud LOD decimation** | Transform-feedback compaction or precomputed Morton-strided per-LOD index buffers | Medium (only if large monolithic LAS is a target) | Medium — A2.7 |
| 8 | **GTAO refinement** over existing HBAO | FS | Low | Medium |

**Not backportable / not candidates:** render bundles, decoupled-lookback scan, subgroup utils, GPU radix/bitonic sort, GPU cull/HiZ (no WebGL2 indirect-draw target). **Already on WebGL — do NOT double-count (A15.1):** OIT-MRT (Scene/OIT.js), AutoExposure, HBAO. Correct the FEATURE_INVENTORY §B tags so a future audit doesn't treat parity features as fork-exclusive; the only genuine WebGPU-only OIT delta (dual-source single-pass) is confirmed never wired.

## 6. Performance & Architecture

**Port-introduced per-frame allocation hot paths (the dominant perf regression vs WebGL's in-place state model):**
- Globe bind groups 0/1/2 per tile per pass (A14.1, HIGH) — root enabler is bindGroup0 binding explicit UB offsets instead of a `hasDynamicOffset:true` BGL (A14.7, MEDIUM).
- Billboard/Label full instance rebuild + full upload per frame (A14.2, HIGH) + dirty-region upload (A14.9, MEDIUM).
- Effects-BG repack + 480-byte writeBuffer + ~20 WeakMap lookups + string-key reconstruction per tile (A14.3 + A14.6, MEDIUM) — primitive path already frame-memoizes; globe doesn't.
- GPU culler reallocates `Float32Array(count*4)` + 24-float plane array per frustum per frame (A14.4, MEDIUM).
- DecoupledScan: fresh bind group + zeros array per dispatch (A10.6, MEDIUM, opt-in).
- Smaller: `computeModifiedModelView` (A1.5), CSM cast SoA dead-write (A7.3), clustered `_scratchEyeLights.slice` (A7.4), CSM Cartesian3 allocs (A7.5), splat slice (A14.5), TAA bind group (A9.7), `sortGaussianSplatsBackToFront` slice (A14.5).

**Adoption gap, not tooling gap (A14.8):** `WebGPUBindGroupCache` (with getStats) is a clean dedup abstraction, but the highest-volume producers bypass it. Surfacing `getStats().hitRate` via CesiumDebug with a 0%-hit-rate flag would have caught these regressions automatically.

**God-objects & sprawl (197-file Renderer/WebGPU tree):**
- `WebGPUContext.ts` 5217 LOC / ~308 fns and `WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts` 4115 LOC remain god-objects despite the 11-slice decomposition — *documented* (WEBGPU_CONTEXT_DECOMPOSITION_PLAN.md); decomposition is losing to feature growth.
- New undecomposed files over the 1000-line guideline: `GlobeTerrain.wgsl` (3799, A1.6), `WebGPUGroundPolylineRenderer.js` (3209), `WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.js` (2873), `WebGPUGroundPrimitiveRenderer.js` (2852) — each embeds multi-KB WGSL template strings inline (A4.5, MEDIUM); `WebGPUPointCloudRenderer.js` (2168, A2.5); `WebGPUModelRenderer.js` (3698).
- **25 untyped `.js` feature renderers = 35,182 LOC** (A16.3, MEDIUM): the WebGPU renderer is only **71% TS by LOC** despite the doc's "all-.ts island" framing — and the *largest, most complex* renderers (Model, GroundPolyline, PrimitiveCommands, GroundPrimitive, ModelPipelineCache) are the least type-safe, the inverse of where `noImplicitAny` is most valuable.
- **Four collection renderers duplicate ~3000 LOC of pipeline-cache / shader-module / placeholder / velocity plumbing with no shared base (A5.3, MEDIUM)** — and the duplication demonstrably drifts (Point gained `needsRebuild`; Billboard/Label didn't → A14.2). Extract a `WebGPUCollectionRendererBase`/helpers.
- **No error sentinels** (re-entry / null-target / buffer-size guards) in any collection renderer despite the CLAUDE.md mandate (A5.4, MEDIUM); silent error-swallow sites in pick pass (A6.7), indirect batch fallback (A12.5), GPU-cull readback (A16.7).
- Per-slice render state smuggled onto `context`/`uniformState` via `as unknown as` casts on a premise (two contexts always differ) that's false in the default single-view path (A12.3, MEDIUM) — introduce a typed `FrustumSliceState`.

**Confirmed-clean (positives):** the `executeCommand`/frustum-loop variant dispatcher is a faithful port (A12.7, no defect); device-loss recovery + SceneRenderer resource invalidation is robust and strictly additive (A12.8); the capability-getter migration is the correct durable replacement for `isWebGPU` branches (A13 — codify it, see §8).

- **Tiles (B3):** I3SNode.js, VoxelEllipsoidShape.js (also collides with an upstream rewrite — priority), Cesium3DTileStyle.js; extract the lone GAUSSIAN_SPLATS line from Cesium3DTile.js surgically.
- **Models (B4):** the ~6 animation/feature conversions (ModelSceneGraph, ModelAnimation, ModelAnimationCollection, CustomShader, ModelFeatureTable, TextureManager, ModelDrawCommand, ClassificationModelDrawCommand).

### Behavioral-risk vs upstream (must-fix regardless of merge strategy)

- **B4 · empty `imageryLayers` guard missing** — port the upstream one-liner *now* (HIGH, affects WebGL).
- **B6 · updateMode ordering/double-call** — restore capability+texture guards to top, drop the redundant second `updateMode` (MEDIUM).
- **B2 · `updateMembers` ctor swap** — restore `updateViewMatrix` (LOW, also needs the import).
- **B5 · WebGL reproject pixel fork** — add a visual-regression tolerance baseline (HIGH-adjacent guard).
- **B10 · Viewer.js pickEntity / Cesium3DTileVectorFeature** — track as must-port at next sync.

### Merge-conflict hotspots (confirmed via `git merge-tree`)

- **Context.js (CONFLICT content) + PickId.js (CONFLICT add/add)** — the only *active* conflicts today.
- **Latent, guaranteed on next upstream touch:** Scene.js, Model.js, Model3DTileContent.js (double-conversion), Globe.js, Cesium3DTileset.js, VoxelEllipsoidShape.js (frozen behind upstream rewrite), EdgeVisibilityPipelineStage.js (hook in gutted function), all 5 collection files, the 6 B5 companion extractions, ShadowMapComputations.js (extraction invisible to upstream).

### Overall drift-refinement recommendation (cheaper future syncs)

1. **Revert the ~15+ pure-cosmetic conversions** above — single biggest lever; eliminates tens of thousands of conflict-lines for zero functional loss.
2. **Adopt a hard guardrail:** class-convert / modernize a file ONLY in the same commit that adds a real WebGPU hook OR a co-located `.d.ts` requires class shape. Add a CI guard that a "modernization-only" diff is empty under `git diff -w`.
3. **Maintain a Scene→companion MOVE-MAP** in the Upstream Sync Procedure (SceneRenderer.js, ShadowMapComputations.js, the 6 B5 helpers, CameraHelpers/Internals) so upstream patches to gutted regions are routed, not re-discovered.
4. **Pre-stage the Context.js/PickId.js merge:** take upstream's PickId.js as base, re-apply `normalizedRgba`/`pickKinds`; align the `@ts-check` header to shrink the hunk.
5. **Restore the stripped public-API JSDoc/@example (Camera/SSCC)** and shadow/camera WHY-comments — they violate the preserve-JSDoc rule and widen the apparent semantic gap at merge.
6. **Never split future modernization into unreviewable mega-commits** — scope, review under `-w`, ship in small commits.

**Intentional WebGPU-specific (no action — correct by design):** the `_alternateSceneRenderer` optional-chaining render hook; the two `isWebGPUDrawCommand` guards (additive, WebGL-safe); the pragma-stripped drillPick `isWebGPU` debug warning; Context.js's 2 no-op compute-extension probes; the edge-emitter single-target fallback; the GPU-cull/HiZ/clustered-lighting/render-bundle/subgroup non-backportable items (§5).

**False-positives (where a reviewer was confused — useful signal):**
- *GlobeDepth depth-copy "divergent RGBA pack"* — not divergent. (A1)
- *Pick-pass drops translucent OIT pick coverage* — not a real gap. (A6)
- *Scene JSDoc "type leak" annotating params as WebGPUContext* — soft annotation, not a leak. (A13)
- *Cesium3DTile extends `depthForTranslucentClassification` to Pass.GAUSSIAN_SPLATS on a WebGL-reachable path* — effectively inert. (B3)
- *`destroyTextureAtlas` accessor as new public-API divergence* — false. (B6)
- *A2.4 (GPU LOD hardcodes Pass.OPAQUE "vs default")* — false premise: the **default** WebGPU PointCloud path *also* hardcodes Pass.OPAQUE, so there's no LOD-vs-default divergence; only the encoder/submit half of that finding is actionable. (A2)
- *A9.5 (edge emitter non-RTE = port regression vs WebGL)* — false: WebGL's edge stage uses the same `czm_modelViewProjection` precision regime; this is a divergence only from WebGPU's *own* RTE main-model path, not a port regression — downgraded to LOW. (A9)

These false-positives cluster around (a) assuming WebGPU diverges from WebGL where WebGL has the *same* limitation, and (b) reading a hardcoded value as a LOD-specific regression when it's a renderer-wide property — worth a reviewer-calibration note.

## Orchestrator verification note (2026-06-11, post-workflow)

The two CRITICAL findings were independently spot-checked against live code by the orchestrating session before publication (CLAUDE.md Principle 8 — do not claim a finding without verifying):

- **NEW-PICKDEPTH-CAPABILITY-READBACK (A6.1) — CONFIRMED REAL.** `WebGPUContext.readPixels` is a *defined* method (WebGPUContext.ts:2533) returning `null`, so `defined(context.readPixels)` is `true` on WebGPU. `PickDepth.update()` (PickDepth.js:103) therefore takes the WebGL framebuffer branch and never sets `_asyncDepthTexture`; `getDepth()` (PickDepth.js:125,148) then returns `undefined`. `pickPosition`/`sampleHeight`/`clampToHeight` depth-readback is broken on WebGPU. The code comment at PickDepth.js:134 ("stub that returns undefined") encodes the author's mistaken premise — it returns `null` but is still *defined*.
- **NEW-OIT-COMPOSITE-FORMAT (A8.1) — CONFIRMED REAL.** `_createCompositePipeline` hardcodes `format: "rgba8unorm"` (WebGPUOIT.ts:295, comment "Will be overridden at draw time" — it never is) and `executeComposite` (WebGPUOIT.ts:222) ignores its `targetFormat` param entirely. Against the default `bgra8unorm` scene color (or `rgba16float` HDR) the MRT-OIT composite fails WebGPU format-match validation. Latent: the MRT-OIT path is fallback-only, so rarely executed in current scenes.

The adversarial-verify stage held up on both top criticals, which calibrates confidence in the broader confirmed-real set (195/235). Medium/low findings were NOT individually re-verified by the orchestrator; treat them as workflow-confirmed pending per-item check at fix time. Full per-finding data (with verdicts): `2026-06-11_ULTRA_REVIEW_findings.json`.
